terra.problem: The joke puts invented words in Solomon’s mouth as a direct quote.
Saying all Papa did in the drawer was lie there contradicts his backstory: he welcomed and helped the other objects.
The passage does not establish that Solomon never hands anything back or that the cities remain in his hands.
Hiram’s identity as king of Tyre is a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
Calling the old drawer empty contradicts Papa’s backstory: it contained papers, dust and his drawer friends.
The text does not say there was no speech or fuss when Solomon captured Hamath-zobah.
The passage says Solomon conscripted the descendants who remained; it does not establish that nobody was sent out.
The passage does not say whether any land was handed over. It says Solomon conscripted these descendants as forced laborers.
The closing lines are flat and generic, adding little beyond repeating that the people had military roles.
The reference to 2 Chronicles 2:3 establishes Hiram as king of Tyre, but it does not say he gave Solomon the cities. That is in 2 Chronicles 8:2.
Hiram’s identity as king of Tyre is a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
Saying the sailors’ experience shows in the result connects their experience to acquiring the gold in a way the text does not.
The statement that cedar comes up elsewhere in Solomon’s story needs a reference.
The passage says the servants acquired gold, but it does not say they brought back no horses.
